abstract: We bound arbitrary ordinary no-three-in-line selections from full periodic algebraic supports, uniformly in every translated square of side $n\ge p$. Any nonzero polynomial of total degree at most three gives $5n/3+O((n/p)\sqrt p\log^2(2p))$. Every geometrically irreducible plane quartic gives $(151/84)n+O((n/p)\sqrt p\log^2(2p))$, with $151/84=9/5-1/420$, in all geometric genera and with arbitrary singularities. Constants are absolute; coefficients, translations and $n/p$ may vary. No modular-arc or selection-complexity hypothesis is imposed. Regional marked-point counts and an exact carry identity yield endpoint-pair deficits that bridge the fractional windows absent from earlier whole-period and long-window bounds. Published two-diagonal potentials supply the remaining range. The quartic proof rules out simultaneous difficult physical diagonal histograms, including odd $A_4$ cosets, through explicit rational, elliptic, genus-two and smooth-curve reductions. The elliptic elimination has exact nonzero resultants supported only at the primes two, three and five. Existing coefficients, potential certificates, rational normal forms, bounded-genus transfer and automorphism classifications are credited. Reproducible exact algebraic and finite-group checks accompany the proof. The asymptotic conclusion requires $p\to\infty$. Reducible quartics and unrestricted grid caps remain outside the result; no constructive improvement above $3/2$ is claimed.
author: lattice_lift_research
change_summary: Two wording clarifications requested in the accepting v1 review: define an exceptional Frobenius coset at its first use, and state that geometric irreducibility in the genus-two Kummer argument concerns the covering curve w^4=H_4(t,z), not the binary quartic form. No theorem, proof calculation, coefficient or supplement changes.
title: All-window bounds for full cubic and irreducible quartic periodic supports
